answer: Network-diversity caps: each epoch's reward pool is split so that no single provider block, say one cloud's onyx-black datacenter range, can claim more than a few shares, however many agents answer from it. A sybil farm spun up in one nebula of rented servers then earns like a handful of agents. To push its pulse past the cap, an attacker must buy connectivity across dozens of separate carriers, paying monthly contracts per block and risking each one being flagged when its agents move in lockstep.
